{"representations":[{"case_ref":"sample_30eeebbcb3af6958","text":"Your March 30–April 12 records show a persistent change in how movement is distributed. Across all 14 days, including weekends, low movement totaled 480 minutes daily versus 449 in your 28-day baseline (+31 minutes, 6.8%). However, individual bouts shortened from 43–47 minutes to 15 minutes, with one-minute movement intervals about every 20 minutes between 10:16 and 20:17. Your 21:00 activity block shortened to 19–28 minutes as movement spread through the day; total active time stayed near 55 minutes.

Steps averaged 8,038 versus 8,026, although they trended downward by about 29 steps/day within the window, with fluctuations. Weekday/weekend activity differences narrowed. Sleep remained near 7 hours 51 minutes (+1 minute), starting around 22:49 and ending consistently at 07:00. Resting heart rate stayed at 55.9 bpm; RMSSD averaged 45.6 versus 45.4 ms, with later dips returning to 47 ms on April 12. Activity and following-night sleep had only a weak association. All metrics were available; low movement does not establish sitting."},{"case_ref":"sample_ee652a22a0edb710","text":"Your recorded active time dropped sharply and stayed lower throughout March 30–April 12: 9.4 minutes/day versus 54.4 in your 28-day baseline (45 minutes less, 83%). Every day had only 8–12 active minutes, concentrated at 21:00, across weekdays and weekends. Meanwhile, low movement rose from 450 to 602 minutes/day (+152 minutes, 34%), in 59–61-minute bouts extending from 10:00 to roughly 20:40–20:53, compared with 43–47-minute baseline bouts. It eased slightly over the fortnight but never returned to baseline.

Steps nevertheless remained essentially unchanged: 8,029 versus 8,015 daily, with little trend or weekday/weekend difference. These measures therefore tell different parts of your movement pattern; steps had only a weak relationship with active minutes.

Sleep stayed near 7 hours 51 minutes, starting around 22:49 and ending at 07:00. Resting heart rate remained near 56 bpm and RMSSD near 45 ms. Active time had only a weak association with following-night sleep, so these records do not establish a sleep effect. No metrics were missing. Checking whether this persistent recording pattern continues would be useful; low movement does not confirm sitting."},{"case_ref":"sample_496a352e5f95a52f","text":"Your sleep changed in two distinct phases. On wake dates March 30–April 5, recorded sleep was 5 hours 57 minutes–6 hours 8 minutes, averaging 6 hours 3 minutes versus your 28-day baseline of 8 hours 1 minute. Sleep started at 00:32–00:43 rather than 22:32–22:46, while waking stayed at 07:00, including weekends. From April 6–12, starts returned to 22:35–22:46 and sleep averaged 8 hours, closely matching baseline. The fortnight average of 7 hours 2 minutes (59 minutes lower) obscures this clear return.

Movement stayed broadly steady: 7,979 versus 7,976 steps/day, 54 versus 56 active minutes, and about 450 low-movement minutes. Activity remained around 21:00; its association with following-night sleep was weak. Weekend steps were somewhat lower than weekdays during this window.

Resting heart rate stayed near 56 bpm. RMSSD averaged 44.2 versus 45.3 ms; it was mostly 43–44 during the first week and more variable afterward, without a consistent return alongside sleep. All measurements were available. Continued recording can show whether the restored sleep timing persists."},{"case_ref":"sample_377d6b28febce198","text":"Your March 30–April 12 records show longer uninterrupted low-movement periods despite stable movement totals. On every day, including weekends, low movement totaled 480 minutes versus your 28-day baseline of 449 (+31 minutes, 6.8%). It occurred in three bouts: 10:00–12:30, 12:45–15:25 and 15:40–18:30, lasting 150–170 minutes each. Baseline bouts lasted 43–47 minutes with five-minute gaps. Low movement does not establish sitting, but this sustained change in bout length is worth tracking.

Active time remained near 55 minutes/day, concentrated at 21:00. Steps averaged 8,038 versus 8,026, although they trended downward about 29 steps/day within the fortnight, with fluctuations. Weekday/weekend movement differences narrowed.

Sleep remained near 7 hours 51 minutes (+1 minute), with starts around 22:49 and waking consistently at 07:00. Resting heart rate stayed at 55.9 bpm; RMSSD averaged 45.6 versus 45.4 ms, with later dips returning to 47 ms on April 12. Activity and following-night sleep had only a weak association; the longer low-movement bouts did not coincide with a sustained shift in these nightly measures. No metrics were missing."}]}
